Isniin, November 23, 2026 (HOL) – Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre, ayaa magacaabay wasiirka cusub ee Gaashaandhigga, isaga oo sidoo kale isku shaandhayn kooban ku sameeyay qaar ka mid ah xubnaha golaha wasiirrada xukuumaddiisa.
War-saxaafadeed ka soo baxay xafiiska Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa lagu sheegay in Saadaq Cumar Maxamed Xasan (Saadaq Joon) loo magacaabay wasiirka Gaashaandhigga, kaddib markii xilkaas uu banneeyay Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo hore u ahaa wasiirka wasaaradda.
Magacaabista Saadaq Joon oo horey u soo noqday taliyihii hore ee ciidanka Booliiska gobolka Banaadir, haatanna ah xildhibaan ka tirsan baarlamaanka Soomaaliya, ayaa magacaabistiisa waxay kusoo beegmaysaa maalin kaddib markii la soo saaray liiska golaha wasiirrada cusub ee maamulka Galmudug.
Magacaabistan ayaa la sheegayaa in ay qayb ka tahay fulinta heshiis siyaasadeed oo saami qeybsi ah oo laga gaaray doorashadii hoggaamiyaha Galmudug, Liibaan Axmed Xasan, kaas oo dhexmaray madaxweynihii hore ee maamulka, Axmed Cabdi Kaariye (Qoor Qoor), iyo dowladda federaalka Soomaaliya.
Dhanka kale, Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamza Cabdi Barre ayaa xilalka isugu beddelay laba xubnood oo ka tirsan golaha wasiirrada. Cali Ifiya Cali ayaa loo magacaabay wasiir ku-xigeenka Wasaaradda Tiknoolajiyadda iyo Gaadiidka Badda, halka Maryan Cali Abuukar loo magacaabay wasiir ku-xigeenka Wasaaradda Kalluumaysiga iyo Dhaqaalaha Buluugga ah.
Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa mas’uuliyiinta cusub faray inay si degdeg ah ula wareegaan xilalka loo magacaabay, isaga oo kula dardaarmay inay waajibaadkooda u gutaan si hufnaan iyo xilkasnimo leh.

Swindon Business Expo returns after heatwave cancellation
A business event cancelled due to the heatwave in June will be returning in freezing temperatures this week, as Swindon prepares to host one of the South West’s biggest business networking gatherings.
The South West Business Expo will take place at the STEAM Museum on Thursday, November 26 – when the thermometer is set to hit zero – from 10am to 3pm, after organisers postponed the original event because of extreme heat.
A health and safety assessment found that indoor temperatures could exceed 36C, making the venue unsuitable for the hundreds of exhibitors, delegates, speakers and staff expected to attend.
Organised by Great British Expos, the rescheduled event has now sold out all 78 exhibition stands.
Businesses from across the South West and beyond will showcase products, services and expertise to hundreds of business owners, entrepreneurs and senior decision-makers.
The free-to-attend expo is aimed at firms of every size, from start-ups and growing SMEs to established regional and national brands. Visitors will be able to meet potential customers, find new suppliers, develop business relationships and explore growth opportunities.
Alongside the exhibition floor, the programme includes keynote speakers, interactive business workshops and dedicated networking sessions.
Organisers say the event will focus on helping South West businesses prepare for growth in 2027 through practical advice, expert insight and face-to-face connections.
Alec Jones-Hall, director of Great British Expos, said the sell-out showed the continued value businesses place on in-person networking.
“We’re absolutely delighted to have sold out all 78 exhibition stands for this Thursday’s event,” he said. “It’s fantastic to see so many businesses investing in face-to-face networking and recognising the opportunities that events like ours can create.”
He added that, with 2027 approaching, the expo offers owners a chance to step away from the office, expand their networks and begin relationships that could generate new business in the year ahead.
“There’s something incredibly valuable about bringing hundreds of ambitious business people together under one roof,” Jones-Hall said. “You never know who you’re going to meet, what opportunities might arise or where a simple conversation could lead.”
Great British Expos has organised regional business exhibitions for more than a decade and says it has welcomed more than 70,000 SMEs to events across the UK. The organisation positions its expos as an accessible alternative to traditional business conferences, combining exhibitions, learning and networking at no cost to visitors.
Although every exhibition stand has been taken, visitor tickets remain available. Organisers are encouraging anyone planning to attend to register in advance.

Deaths linked to heat pass a record 5,000 in England this year, data shows
More than 5,000 deaths were linked to heat in England this year, the highest since current records began in 2016, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has said.
An estimated 5,258 deaths were associated with hot weather, comfortably beating the previous high of 2,985 set in 2022.
The year saw the UK experience its warmest summer on record, with parts of the country enduring multiple heatwaves over several months, beginning in late May when temperatures peaked at 35.1C at Kew Gardens in London, an all-time high for the month.
The heatwave at the end of June prompted a rare red alert from the Met Office for extreme heat and saw temperatures reach 38.0C on June 26 in Lingwood in Norfolk, another new monthly record.
As the scorching summer continued, England saw its driest July since data began, with only 7mm of rain measured, or 10% of the long-term average.
The heatwave in mid-August saw temperatures climb as high as 38.2C at Hartpury College in Gloucestershire, making it the hottest day of the year.
In its report, the UKHSA said: “Summer 2026 was an exceptional summer with the highest mortality observed since 2016 when the UKHSA began publishing annual heat mortality reports.
“Significant mortality impacts were observed early in the summer season, with over 3,000 estimated heat-associated deaths across the May and June heat episodes.”
The highest number of heat-associated deaths were recorded between June 21 and 28, when an estimated 2,401 deaths were linked to this period of extreme heat.
This year’s total of 5,258 deaths follows a run of much lower annual totals, with 2,295 in 2023, 1,311 in 2024 and 1,504 in 2025.
The report said intense heat early in the summer season “can pose particular risks as unusually hot weather may occur before people, communities and services have fully prepared and are ready to respond to hot weather conditions”.
It added: “These findings therefore reinforce the importance of heat-health preparedness measures being in place from the start of the season, rather than focusing solely on the warmest periods of mid-summer.”
Dr Ross Thompson, principal environmental health scientist at the UKHSA, said: “Heat can affect anyone, but older adults, young children, pregnant women and people with underlying health conditions are at greater risk.
“Climate change is already affecting people’s health in England, and as the climate continues to warm we can expect periods of extreme heat to become longer, more frequent and more intense.
“That is why it is vital that individuals, communities, health and care services and local organisations are prepared, not just during a heatwave but in the longer term.
“The decisions we make now will shape the health impacts people experience in the decades ahead.”
